title: Nested Routes & Folder Structure
description: Create sub-folders to build nested URLs like /blog/post-1 – just like organising your files.

slides.title: Organising Your Pages 📂
slides.content:
# Think of folders as route segments

If your site has a blog section with many posts, you can group them:

```
pages/
  blog/
    first-post.js
    second-post.js
```

* `/blog/first-post`
* `/blog/second-post`

Clean and logical – just like your file explorer!

slides.title: Creating a Blog Post (pages/blog/first-post.js)
slides.content: Any nested file works the same way. Export a default component.

quizData.question: If you move `pages/about.js` into a new folder `pages/company/about.js`, what URL does it now generate?
quizData.explanation: The folder structure adds a segment. `company/about.js` → `/company/about`.

slides.title: The Root of a Folder 🏠
slides.content:
# What about the folder itself?

Often you need a page for the folder root, like `/blog` listing all posts.

* Use `index.js` inside the folder.

`pages/blog/index.js` → **`/blog`**

The `index` file serves as the **default** for that route segment.

slides.title: Blog Index (pages/blog/index.js)
slides.content: Now `/blog` renders a list of posts while `/blog/first-post` shows a single post.

quizData.question: Which file creates the route `/dashboard`?

options.text: Both A and B are valid

quizData.explanation: Both `pages/dashboard.js` and `pages/dashboard/index.js` would map to `/dashboard`, but they cannot coexist. If both exist, `dashboard.js` wins (see next lesson).
